title: auth_jwt Module
content_markdown: The module implements authentication over JSON Web Tokens. In some cases ( ie. WebRTC ) the user authenticates on another layer ( other than SIP ), so it makes no sense to double-authenticate it on the SIP layer. Thus, the SIP client will simply present the JWT auth token it received from the server, and pass it on to OpenSIPS which will use that for authentication purposes.
overview: The module implements authentication over JSON Web Tokens. In some cases ( ie. WebRTC ) the user authenticates on another layer ( other than SIP ), so it makes no sense to double-authenticate it on the SIP layer. Thus, the SIP client will simply present the JWT auth token it received from the server, and pass it on to OpenSIPS which will use that for authentication purposes.
how_it_works: It relies on two DB tables, one containing JWT profiles ( a profile name and it's SIP username associated to it ) and one containing JWT secrets. Each secret has a corresponding profile, the KEY used for signing the JWT and two timestamps describing a validation interval. Multiple JWT secrets can point to the same JWT profile.

dependencies_required.name: database
dependencies_required.reason: Any database module (currently mysql, postgres, dbtext), required if db_url parameter is set.

exported_parameters.name: db_mode
exported_parameters.description: If set to 0, the module won't connect to the Database for reading the Keys for decoding JWTs - only jwt\_script\_authorize will be usable from the script.

exported_parameters.name: db_url
exported_parameters.description: This is URL of the database to be used. Value of the parameter depends on the database module used. For example for mysql and postgres modules this is something like mysql://username:password@host:port/database. For dbtext module (which stores data in plaintext files) it is directory in which the database resides.

exported_parameters.name: profiles_table
exported_parameters.description: Name of the DB table containing the jwt profiles

exported_parameters.name: secrets_table
exported_parameters.description: Name of the DB table containing the jwt secrets

exported_parameters.name: tag_column
exported_parameters.description: Column holding the JWT profile tag.

exported_parameters.name: username_column
exported_parameters.description: Column holding the JWT profile associated SIP username.

exported_parameters.name: secret_tag_column
exported_parameters.description: Column holding the JWT secret associated tag.

exported_parameters.name: secret_column
exported_parameters.description: Column holding the actual jwt signing secret.

exported_parameters.name: start_ts_column
exported_parameters.description: Column holding the JWT secret start UNIX timestamp.

exported_parameters.name: end_ts_column
exported_parameters.description: column holding the jwt secret end unix timestamp.

exported_parameters.name: tag_claim
exported_parameters.description: The JWT claim which will be used to identify the JWT profile

exported_parameters.name: load_credentials
exported_parameters.description:
This parameter specifies credentials to be fetched from the JWT profiles table when the authentication is performed. The loaded credentials will be stored in AVPs. If the AVP name is not specificaly given, it will be used a NAME AVP with the same name as the column name.

Parameter syntax:

*   _load_credentials = credential (';' credential)*_
    
*   _credential = (avp_specification '=' column_name) | (column_name)_
    
*   _avp_specification = '$avp(' + NAME + ')'_

exported_functions.name: jwt_db_authorize

parameters.name: jwt_token
parameters.description: The JWT token to perform auth on. The string may contain pseudo variables.

parameters.name: out_decoded_token
parameters.description: PVAR used to store the decoded JWT upon succesful auth

parameters.name: out_sip_username
parameters.description: PVAR used to store the SIP username corresponding to the JWT profile, upon succesful auth

exported_functions.description: The function will read the first param ( jwt_token ), extract the tag claim and then try to authenticate it against the DB secrets for the respective profile tag. In case of success, it populates the out_decoded_token pvar with the decoded JWT ( in plaintext format header_json.payload_json ) and the out_sip_username with the SIP username corresponding to that JWT profile.

exported_functions.name: jwt_script_authorize

parameters.name: jwt_token
parameters.description: The JWT token to perform auth on. The string may contain pseudo variables.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: The key to be used for validating the JWT.

parameters.name: out_decoded_token
parameters.description: PVAR used to store the decoded JWT

return_values.condition: Failure in decoding the JWT (out_decoded_token will not be populated)
Failure in validating the JWT (out_decoded_token will be populated)
JWT succesfully validated with the key (out_decoded_token will be populated)

exported_functions.description: The function will read the first param ( jwt_token ), decode it and then try to validate it against the provided key. If the JWT decoding is succesful, the out_decoded_token pvar will be populated.

exported_functions.name: extract_pub_key_from_cert

parameters.name: certificate
parameters.description: The certificate to read and from which to extract the public key. The string may contain pseudo variables.

parameters.name: out_public_key
parameters.description: PVAR used to store the extracted public key

return_values.condition: Failure in extracting the pub key

exported_functions.description: The function will read the first param ( certificate ), decode it and then try to extract the public key with the certificate. If the extraction is succesful, the out_public_key will be populated. Useful to be used in conjuction with the jwt_script_authorize function, since most providers make their certificates public, but the JWTs are signed with the actual public key embeded in the certificate.
